title: Armada: The Open Source, Encrypted Discord Alternative | Soapbox
excerpt: A free, open source, end-to-end encrypted Discord alternative: servers, channels, voice, and moderation, with no company in the middle. Now in open beta.
content_html:
Voice and video calls, custom emojis, GIFs, and more.

Self-hostable at every level.

Communities are decentralized by default. When you want more independence, every piece runs on your own hardware. Take one piece or all three; the self-hosting guide walks through each one.

Self-host the client

Serve the web app from your own domain. armada →

Self-host a relay

Keep encrypted messages on a relay you run. ditto-relay →

Self-host voice

Route calls through your own LiveKit box. armada-av →

Open protocol · no lock-in

Interoperable with other Nostr apps.

Armada is built on Nostr and supports multiple formats including Concord, NIP-29, and Buzz communities. One key logs you in across the ecosystem, and where clients share protocols, your communities and DMs come with you.

Frequently asked questions

Is Armada a good Discord alternative?

If you have used Discord, you already know the layout: communities, channels, threads, voice, and moderation. The difference is underneath. Every community is end-to-end encrypted, your account is a key instead of an email, and communities live on many relays at once, so no company can ban you or delete your server. Read the full comparison.

Is Armada free?

Yes. Armada is free and open source under the AGPL-3.0 license, with no ads and no paid tier.

Can I be banned from Armada?

There is no company account to ban. Community owners moderate their own spaces, but no one can delete your identity or take your community down across all of its relays.

Do I need a phone number or email to sign up?

No. Signing up generates a cryptographic key, and that key is your whole account, on Armada and across every other Nostr app. How to store your key.

Does Armada work on iPhone?

There is no iOS app yet. The web app at armada.buzz works on iPhone, and native apps exist for Android, macOS, Linux, and Windows.

Is Armada ready to use?

Armada is in open beta ahead of its v1.0 release. Communities, encrypted DMs, and voice and video calls all work today, with new releases landing almost daily. Expect occasional rough edges while it matures.
